SEO is ongoing work that helps search engines understand, discover, and present web content.·A help article that truly answers a question with clear headings, body structure, and reachable links is easier for search systems to understand; product pages also need accessible content and links. Which foundations SEO improves

Content answers a real question first: A page needs useful, accurate content. Its title and sections tell people and search systems what it solves; keyword stuffing or vague promotion cannot replace an answer.

Crawlers read pages through links and HTML: Search engines follow links to discover pages and read title, meta description, heading structure, and image alt attributes. Pure client-rendered apps with empty initial HTML may hide content from crawlers.

AI-generated pages often need SEO polish: AI often misses unique titles and meta descriptions, single-h1 hierarchy, image alt text, and semantic HTML (article, nav, main). Check and fix these basics before launching.

What it is not

SEO is neither buying rank nor changing a few keywords. Results depend on query intent, competition, quality, and system judgment among other factors. Clear content and technical accessibility are necessary work but cannot promise traffic or position.
